hints.S47_A1: Friendship is compared to GOLD, and the dash spells it out: RARE and WORTH PROTECTING. Ask: which word means highly valuable? 'Heavy' weighs gold, 'common' is the opposite of rare, and 'dull' has nothing to do with worth.
hints.S47_A2: Lena FORGOT HER LUNCH, so the friend passed HALF OF HER SANDWICH straight to her. Ask: which phrasal verb means to give something to another person? 'Threw away' bins it, 'gave up' means stopped trying, 'broke off' only snaps a piece.
hints.S47_A3: OTHERS WALK AWAY, but a TRUE FRIEND does the opposite. Ask: which phrasal verb means to stay loyally beside someone in hard times? 'Ignore', 'criticise' and 'avoid' all describe leaving a person alone.
hints.S47_A4: They AGREED TO MOVE ON after their ARGUMENT, so the quarrel is over. Ask: which verb means to settle a disagreement? 'Deepened' would make it worse, 'ignored' leaves it unsettled, and 'remembered' changes nothing.
hints.S47_A5: You give away your LAST BISCUIT to a HUNGRY CLASSMATE and get nothing back. Ask: which word describes putting another person's needs before your own? 'Ordinary' clashes with 'small BUT ___', which promises something admirable.
hints.S47_B1: The subject is SOMEONE - one unknown person, however many it might have been. Ask: does a singular subject take 'have', or the helping verb ending in -s? 'Are' and 'were' cannot partner LEFT in this pattern at all.
hints.S47_B2: HAVE is already there, so the blank must complete a present perfect that started in PRIMARY ONE and is still true. Ask: after 'have', which form of the verb 'be' do we use - the plain one, the -ing one, or the past participle?
hints.S47_B3: MORE GENEROUS is already a comparative, so the blank must strengthen it. Ask: can 'very', 'too' or another 'more' ever stand in front of a comparative? Only one small word is allowed there, and it means 'by a long way'.
hints.S47_B4: The interruption is clear: a TEACHER SUDDENLY WALKED IN. Ask: at that moment, had the girls finished the job, or was it still going on? Pick the past form that keeps an action running until something cuts across it.
hints.S47_B5: KINDNESS cannot be counted - you cannot have one kindness, two kindnesses. Ask: which word partners an uncountable noun? 'A few', 'many' and 'several' all need things you can count, like umbrellas.
hints.S47_B6: Count what the tag must copy: the helping verb HAVE, nothing else - so 'didn't' and 'weren't' are impossible before you start. Ask: when the statement is positive, which way must the tag flip?
hints.S47_B7: An AWARD cannot hand itself out; it goes TO A STUDENT, and the school does the giving. Ask: which choice makes the subject the RECEIVER of the action, in past time? Two of the options are active, and one is present.
hints.S47_B8: TOLD THE STUDENTS = a reported instruction. Ask: after 'told + person', does the verb appear plain, with -ing, with -ed, or with 'to' in front? Only one of those four patterns is used to report an instruction.
hints.S47_C1: The blank is the subject of HAVE BEEN, and the sentence goes on 'since WE were in KINDERGARTEN' - the speaker is one of that 'we'. Ask: does the doer of an action take the subject form or the object form?
hints.S47_C2: Look at the word right after the blank: BIRTHDAY, a noun - and the birthday belongs to the person telling the story. Ask: which form of a pronoun goes in FRONT of a noun to show ownership? The object form cannot.
hints.S47_C3: Nobody helped - the card was made INSTEAD OF BUYING ONE FROM THE SHOP. Ask: when the doer and the person referred to are the same, which family of pronouns do we reach for? A plain object form cannot end this sentence.
hints.S47_C4: The blank is the subject of SAW, and it stands for SITI, one girl. Ask: does the doer of a verb take the subject form or the object form? 'Her saw the card' is never English.
hints.S47_C5: The blank comes straight after the verb HELPED, so it RECEIVES the action - it is not the doer. Ask: after a verb, do we use the subject form or the object form? 'Helped she' is never English.
hints.S47_C6: The little word AT sits right in front of the blank, and the person laughing (SITI) is not the person being laughed at. Ask: after a preposition, which form of the pronoun do we use - the doer form, or the receiver form?
hints.S47_C7: The blank is the subject of ARE THE ONES YOU CAN CALL, and it stands for GOOD FRIENDS - more than one person. Ask: which pronoun can begin a clause as the doer? 'Them are the ones' is never English.
hints.S47_C8: Real friends never need to PRETEND - so around each other they can be their own true selves. Ask: when the subject and the people described are the same, which ending does the pronoun take? A plain object form cannot follow 'be' here.
hints.S47_D1: The dash defines it: GENUINE CARE FOR ANOTHER PERSON'S FEELINGS. Ask: which box word names that deep feeling for someone who is suffering? It must be a noun, because 'requires' needs a thing after it.
hints.S47_D2: The clue follows the dash: THEY STAY BY YOUR SIDE EVEN WHEN THINGS ARE HARD. Ask: which box word describes a friend who never abandons you? It must be a describing word, since it follows 'is also'.
hints.S47_D3: This friend TELLS YOU THE TRUTH KINDLY, rather than saying whatever you want to hear. Ask: which box word means honest and genuine? Other box words describe people too, so match the meaning to the TRUTH.
hints.S47_D4: The blank follows THE ABILITY TO, so it must be a plain verb, and ARGUMENTS have just happened. Ask: which box word means to stop being angry with someone who hurt you? 'Betray' would end a friendship, not keep it alive.
hints.S47_D5: The blank sits between A STRONG and OF TRUST, so it is a noun, and it GROWS BETWEEN TWO PEOPLE. Ask: which box word names the invisible link that ties two friends together?
hints.S47_E1: The underlined word takes -ED, but TEACH is irregular and never does. Ask: how would you say it in the past - 'yesterday she ___ us a song'? Compare catch and buy: they change their middle instead of adding an ending.
hints.S47_E2: The subject is THE PUPILS - a whole class, not one child. Ask: which past form of 'to be' goes with a plural subject? The verb must agree with the subject, not with the mood of the sentence.
hints.S47_E3: The underlined word has swapped two vowels. Ask: does the rhyme say I before E, or E before I, when no C stands in front? Check the middle of 'FREIND' against field, piece and chief.
hints.S47_E4: The verb SHARED needs a word that says HOW the sharing was done. Ask: which word class describes an action - the adjective, which belongs to nouns, or the adverb? Listen for the -ly ending.
hints.S47_E5: The drawings belong to the STUDENTS - all of them, not one. Ask: when a plural noun already ends in -s, where does the apostrophe go, and do you add another s after it? A single owner would be different.
hints.S47_F1: AS LONG AS introduces the CONDITION, so it must stand in front of the fact that has to be true first. Ask: does a condition clause ever take 'will'? Decide which fact is the requirement and which is the promise.
hints.S47_F2: ALTHOUGH marks the fact that makes the next one surprising. Ask: which fact should follow ALTHOUGH - the noticing, or the sitting in silence? The second half then needs a pronoun, so the GIRL is not named twice.
